questions.text: कबीर ने एक प्रसिद्ध कार व्यापारी, 'ग्लोबल मोटर्स' से ₹ 2 करोड़ की एक आरामदायक (लक्जरी) कार खरीदी । कुछ ही दिनों में, उसने कार में गंभीर कमियाँ पाईं । जब उसने 'ग्लोबल मोटर्स' से सम्पर्क किया, तो उन्होंने कार को ठीक करने या बदलने से मना कर दिया । कबीर ने तब उपयुक्त उपभोक्ता न्यायालय में केस दर्ज करवाया । लेकिन इस न्यायालय के आदेश से कबीर संतुष्ट नहीं हुआ । अब कबीर कहाँ अपील दर्ज कर सकता है ?
questions.text_english: Kabir purchased a luxury car for ₹ 2 crores from a well-known car dealer named 'Global Motors'. Within a few days, he found serious defects in the car. When he contacted 'Global Motors', they refused to repair or replace the car. Kabir then filed a case in the appropriate consumer court. However, he was not satisfied with the orders of this court. Where can Kabir file an appeal now ?

options.B: राज्य कमीशन
options.C: राष्ट्रीय कमीशन
options.D: सुप्रीम कोर्ट

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) State Commission. Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the three-tier consumer dispute redressal mechanism works in a hierarchical manner. Since the car costs ₹2 crores, the case would have originally been filed in the State Commission (which handles complaints involving goods/services worth more than ₹1 crore but up to ₹10 crores). However, the question states that Kabir filed in the 'appropriate' court and was dissatisfied, implying he filed in the District Commission. An appeal against the District Commission's order lies with the State Commission. Option (A) District Commission is the court whose order he is unhappy with. Option (C) National Commission handles appeals from State Commission orders. Option (D) Supreme Court is the final appellate authority, not the immediate next step.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) राज्य कमीशन है। उपभोक्ता संरक्षण अधिनियम, 2019 के अंतर्गत तीन-स्तरीय उपभोक्ता विवाद निवारण प्रणाली है। जिला आयोग के आदेश से असंतुष्ट उपभोक्ता राज्य आयोग में अपील कर सकता है। राज्य आयोग के आदेश के विरुद्ध राष्ट्रीय आयोग में और राष्ट्रीय आयोग के आदेश के विरुद्ध सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में अपील की जा सकती है।

questions.text: शरद, 'नोवा लिमिटेड' में प्रचालन प्रबंधक था । उसने उत्पादन पर्यवेक्षक, अनिता को एक अतिआवश्यक आदेश की पूर्ति करने का कार्य सौंपा । उसे कार्य की योजना बनाने तथा निश्चित समय सीमा में उसे पूरा करने का अधिकार दिया । अनिता ने उस कार्य को आगे मशीन प्रचालक, रोहित को सौंप दिया और उसे दिन के अंत तक पूरा करने को कहा । रोहित कार्य को समय पर पूरा नहीं कर सका जिसके कारण कम्पनी आदेश की सुपुर्दगी करने में असफल रही । कार्य पूरा न होने पर शरद के प्रति कौन उत्तरदायी है ?
questions.text_english: Sharad was the Operations Manager at 'Nova Ltd.' He assigned the task of completing an urgent order to Anita, the Production Supervisor. She was given the authority to plan the work and meet the deadline. Anita further assigned the work to Rohit, a machine operator and asked him to finish it by the end of the day. Rohit did not complete the task on time, due to which the company failed to deliver the order. Who is accountable to Sharad for non-completion of the work ?

options.B: अनिता
options.C: रोहित एवं अनिता दोनों
options.D: स्वयं शरद

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Anita. This question tests the concept of accountability in delegation. A fundamental principle of delegation is that authority can be delegated but accountability cannot. Sharad delegated the task to Anita and gave her the authority. Anita is therefore accountable to Sharad for the completion of the task, even though she further delegated it to Rohit. While Rohit is answerable to Anita, Anita alone remains accountable to Sharad. Option (A) is incorrect because Rohit has no direct accountability to Sharad. Option (C) is incorrect because accountability flows directly between Sharad and the person he delegated to, which is Anita only. Option (D) is incorrect as Sharad delegated the work.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) अनिता है। प्रत्यायोजन का एक मूल सिद्धांत यह है कि प्राधिकार का प्रत्यायोजन किया जा सकता है, परंतु जवाबदेही का नहीं। शरद ने अनिता को कार्य सौंपा था, इसलिए अनिता ही शरद के प्रति जवाबदेह है। अनिता आगे रोहित को कार्य सौंप सकती है, परंतु वह शरद के प्रति उत्तरदायित्व से मुक्त नहीं होती।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित कथनों को पढ़िए : अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) ।
अभिकथन (A) : अभिप्रेरणा सकारात्मक हो सकती है अथवा नकारात्मक ।
कारण (R) : व्यक्ति अपनी अपेक्षाओं, धारणाओं और प्रतिक्रियाओं में भिन्न-भिन्न होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Read the following statements : Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Motivation can be either positive or negative.
Reason (R) : Individuals are heterogeneous in their expectations, perceptions and reactions.
questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose the correct alternative from the options given below :

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों असत्य हैं।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है, परंतु कारण (R) असत्य है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). The Assertion (A) is true — motivation can indeed be positive (e.g., incentives, promotions, praise) or negative (e.g., fear of punishment, demotion). The Reason (R) is also true — individuals do differ in their expectations, perceptions and reactions, which is a well-established principle in motivation theory. However, the Reason (R) does not correctly explain the Assertion (A). The reason why motivation can be positive or negative is not because individuals are heterogeneous, but rather because motivation techniques themselves are of two types — those that offer rewards (positive) and those that use threats or punishments (negative). The heterogeneity of individuals explains why different motivational approaches are needed for different people, which is a separate concept.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। अभिकथन (A) सत्य है — अभिप्रेरणा सकारात्मक या नकारात्मक दोनों प्रकार की हो सकती है। कारण (R) भी सत्य है — व्यक्ति अपनी अपेक्षाओं, धारणाओं और प्रतिक्रियाओं में भिन्न होते हैं। परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता, क्योंकि अभिप्रेरणा के सकारात्मक या नकारात्मक होने का कारण व्यक्तियों की विभिन्नता नहीं, बल्कि प्रेरणा की तकनीकें हैं।

questions.text:
'नियोजन में दूरदर्शिता, बुद्धिमत्तापूर्ण कल्पना और सुदृढ़ निर्णय से युक्त मस्तिष्क के अनुप्रयोग की आवश्यकता होती है ।'
उपर्युक्त कथन में प्रतिबिंबित नियोजन की विशेषता है :
questions.text_english:
'Planning requires application of mind involving foresight, intelligence imagination and sound judgement.'
The feature of planning reflected by the above statement is :

options.B: नियोजन में निर्णयन निहित है
options.C: नियोजन एक मानसिक अभ्यास है
options.D: नियोजन अविरत है

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Planning is a mental exercise. The statement specifically emphasises the use of mind and mental faculties such as foresight, intelligence, imagination and sound judgement. This directly points to the feature that planning is a mental exercise — it is not a physical activity but an intellectual one requiring thinking, reasoning and deliberation. Option (A) is incorrect because being futuristic refers to planning being concerned with future events, not the application of mental faculties. Option (B) is incorrect because decision-making refers to selecting from alternatives, which is a part of planning but not what the statement highlights. Option (D) is incorrect because continuity refers to planning being a never-ending process.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) नियोजन एक मानसिक अभ्यास है। दिए गए कथन में दूरदर्शिता, बुद्धि, कल्पना और निर्णय जैसे मानसिक गुणों पर जोर दिया गया है, जो यह दर्शाता है कि नियोजन एक मानसिक क्रिया है, शारीरिक नहीं।

questions.text:
'व्यावसायिक पर्यावरण एक देश से दूसरे देश तथा एक क्षेत्र से दूसरे क्षेत्र में भिन्न-भिन्न होता है ।'
उपर्युक्त कथन में प्रतिबिंबित व्यावसायिक पर्यावरण की विशेषता है :
questions.text_english:
'The business environment differs from country to country and even region to region.'
The feature of business environment reflected in the above statement is :

options.B: जटिलता
options.C: अनिश्चितता
options.D: गतिशील प्रकृति

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Relativity. The statement highlights that the business environment is not the same everywhere — it varies from country to country and region to region. This variation or relative difference is captured by the feature of Relativity, which means business environment is a relative concept as it differs from place to place and from time to time. Option (B) Complexity refers to the large number of inter-related and interdependent factors. Option (C) Uncertainty refers to difficulty in predicting future changes. Option (D) Dynamic nature refers to the business environment being constantly changing, not that it differs geographically.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) सापेक्षता है। दिया गया कथन यह दर्शाता है कि व्यावसायिक पर्यावरण एक स्थान से दूसरे स्थान पर भिन्न होता है, जो सापेक्षता की विशेषता को इंगित करता है।

questions.text: नीचे दर्शाए गए पाउच में चिप्स के विभिन्न स्वादों के पैकेट सम्मिलित हैं। पाउच की पैकेजिंग के स्तर को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: The pouch depicted below contains packets of different flavours of chips. Identify the level of packaging of the pouch :

options.B: द्वितीयक
options.C: परिवहन
options.D: साधारण

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Secondary. In packaging, the primary package is the one that directly contains the product (individual chips packets). The secondary package is the one that holds together several primary packages — in this case, the large transparent pouch containing multiple individual chips packets is the secondary level of packaging. It is used for grouping and display purposes. Option (C) Transportation packaging is a third level used for bulk storage and shipping, such as large cartons or crates used by wholesalers.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) द्वितीयक है। प्राथमिक पैकेजिंग वह है जो सीधे उत्पाद को बंद करती है (यहाँ प्रत्येक चिप्स का पैकेट)। द्वितीयक पैकेजिंग वह है जो कई प्राथमिक पैकेजों को एक साथ रखती है — यहाँ बड़ा पारदर्शी पाउच द्वितीयक पैकेजिंग है।

questions.text: व्यावसायिक पर्यावरण के महत्त्व के संबंध में गलत कथन को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the incorrect statement with respect to the importance of business environment :

options.A: यह तीव्रता से हो रहे परिवर्तनों का सामना करने में सहायता करता है
options.B: यह उपयोगी संसाधनों का दोहन (उपयोग) करने में सहायता करता है
options.C: यह नियोजन एवं नीति निर्धारण में सहायता करता है
options.D: यह राजनैतिक अस्थिरता को बढ़ाने में सहायता करता है और फलस्वरूप दीर्घकालीन परियोजनाओं में निवेश के लिए लोगों में आत्मविश्वास का निर्माण करता है

options_english.A: It helps in coping with rapid changes
options_english.B: It helps in tapping useful resources
options_english.C: It helps in assisting in planning and policy formulation
options_english.D: It helps in increasing political instability and thus build the confidence of people to invest in long term projects

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D), which is the incorrect statement. Understanding the business environment actually helps in identifying political stability — a stable political environment builds investor confidence to invest in long-term projects. The statement in option (D) is factually wrong because understanding the business environment does not 'increase political instability'; rather, awareness of a stable political environment encourages long-term investment. Options (A), (B), and (C) are all correct statements about the importance of business environment: it helps firms cope with rapid changes, tap useful resources, and assist in planning and policy-making.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है जो गलत कथन है। व्यावसायिक पर्यावरण का ज्ञान राजनीतिक अस्थिरता को बढ़ावा नहीं देता, बल्कि यह व्यवसायियों को राजनीतिक स्थिरता की पहचान करने में मदद करता है जिससे दीर्घकालीन निवेश का आत्मविश्वास बनता है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित कथनों को पढ़िए : अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) ।
अभिकथन (A) : एक फर्म की ऋण की लागत समता की लागत से अधिक होती है ।
कारण (R) : ऋणदाता का जोखिम समता अंशधारियों के जोखिम से कम होता है, क्योंकि ऋणदाता को सुनिश्चित प्रतिफल और पूँजी की वापसी प्राप्त होती है ।
questions.text_english:
Read the following statements : Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The cost of debt is higher than the cost of equity for a firm.
Reason (R) : The lender's risk is lower than the equity shareholder's risk, since the lender earns an assured return and repayment of capital.
questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose the correct alternative from the options given below :

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है, परंतु कारण (R) असत्य है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) असत्य है, परंतु कारण (R) सत्य है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The Assertion (A) is false: in reality, the cost of debt is generally lower than the cost of equity. This is because lenders face lower risk — they receive assured interest and repayment of principal regardless of the company's profits. Since lenders take less risk, they accept a lower return, making debt cheaper for the firm. Additionally, interest on debt is tax-deductible, which further reduces its effective cost. The Reason (R) is true — the lender's risk is indeed lower than that of equity shareholders because lenders receive assured returns and repayment of capital. Thus, (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। अभिकथन (A) असत्य है — वास्तव में एक फर्म के लिए ऋण की लागत समता की लागत से कम होती है, क्योंकि ऋण पर ब्याज कर-कटौती योग्य होता है और ऋणदाता को सुनिश्चित प्रतिफल मिलता है। कारण (R) सत्य है।

questions.text:
सितम्बर, 2025 में 'कोजी गारमेन्ट्स' ने जैकेट बनाना आरम्भ किया । वे सर्दी के मौसम में जैकेट्स की माँग में वृद्धि अनुमानित कर रहे थे। बढ़े हुए कार्यभार को सँभालने के लिए, उत्पादन प्रबंधक ने चरम उत्पादन दिनों में आवश्यक कर्मचारियों की संख्या का अनुमान लगाया और उसी के अनुसार योजना बनाई ।
उपर्युक्त स्थिति में योजना के जिस प्रकार पर प्रकाश डाला गया है, वह है :
questions.text_english:
'Cosy Garments' started the manufacturing of jackets in September, 2025. They expected a rise in the demand for jackets during the winter season. To handle the increased workload, the Production Manager estimated the number of workers required during peak production days and planned accordingly.
The type of plan highlighted in the above case is :

options.B: नीति
options.C: विधि
options.D: उद्देश्य

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Budget. A budget is a statement of expected results expressed in numerical terms for a specific period of time. In this case, the Production Manager estimated the number of workers required during peak production days — this is essentially a numerical estimate or quantitative plan, which is a budget (specifically a manpower/labour budget). Option (B) Policy is a set of general guidelines for decision-making. Option (C) Method refers to the prescribed ways of performing a specific task. Option (D) Objective refers to the end points or goals to be achieved.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) बजट है। बजट एक ऐसी योजना है जो संख्यात्मक रूप में अपेक्षित परिणामों को व्यक्त करती है। यहाँ उत्पादन प्रबंधक ने चरम उत्पादन दिनों में आवश्यक कर्मचारियों की संख्या का अनुमान लगाया — यह श्रम/मानव-शक्ति बजट है।

questions.text:
'ऐग्री सोल्यूशन्स', एक तेजी से विकसित हो रही कृषि-तकनीकी कंपनी, लगातार कर्मचारियों द्वारा संगठन को छोड़कर जाने की समस्या का सामना कर रही थी । नतीजन, काम प्रभावित हो रहा था और समय व धन बार-बार भर्ती एवं प्रशिक्षण पर खर्च हो रहा था । जाँच-पड़ताल में यह पाया गया कि समस्या का कारण यह था कि कर्मचारियों को अपनी नई भूमिका में स्थापित होने का पर्याप्त समय नहीं मिल पा रहा था । अत: कंपनी ने निर्णय लिया कि वह अपने कर्मचारियों को कम-से-कम एक निश्चित अवधि के लिए एक ही स्थिति (पद) में रखेंगे तथा परिणाम दर्शाने के लिए उन्हें पर्याप्त समय दिया जाएगा । इससे कर्मचारी आवर्तन में महत्त्वपूर्ण कमी आई और संगठनात्मक कार्यक्षमता में सुधार हुआ ।
उपर्युक्त स्थिति में प्रबंध के जिस सिद्धांत पर प्रकाश डाला गया है, वह है :
questions.text_english:
'Agri Solutions', a fast-growing agri-tech company, was facing a problem of employees leaving the organisation frequently. As a result, work suffered and time and money were spent repeatedly on recruitment and training. On investigation, it was found that the problem was due to employees not getting sufficient time to settle into their new roles. So the company decided to keep their employees at the same position for a minimum tenure and give them sufficient time to show results. This led to a significant reduction in employee turnover and improvement in organisational efficiency.
The principle of management highlighted in the above case is :

options.B: कर्मचारियों की स्थिरता
options.C: कार्य-विभाजन
options.D: अधिकार एवं उत्तरदायित्व

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Stability of Personnel. Fayol's principle of Stability of Personnel states that employees should be given a reasonable tenure so they can settle into their roles and perform effectively. High employee turnover is harmful to the organisation because it increases costs of recruitment and training and disrupts workflows. The case of 'Agri Solutions' perfectly illustrates this — by providing employees sufficient time at the same position, the company reduced turnover and improved efficiency. Option (A) Order refers to the right place for the right person/material. Option (C) Division of Work refers to specialisation of tasks. Option (D) Authority and Responsibility refers to maintaining a balance between the two.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) कर्मचारियों की स्थिरता है। फेयोल का यह सिद्धांत कहता है कि कर्मचारियों को अपनी भूमिका में स्थापित होने के लिए उचित समय दिया जाना चाहिए। इससे संगठन की कार्यक्षमता बढ़ती है और कर्मचारी आवर्तन कम होता है।

questions.text: _____________ एक रूपरेखा है जिसके अंतर्गत प्रबन्धकीय तथा संचालन संबंधी कार्यों को निष्पादित किया जाता है ।
questions.text_english: _____________ is the framework within which the managerial and operating tasks are performed.

options.B: संगठन ढाँचा
options.C: अंतरण
options.D: विकेन्द्रीकरण

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Organisational structure. An organisational structure is a formal framework that defines how activities such as task allocation, coordination, and supervision are directed towards achieving organisational goals. It acts as a framework within which all managerial and operational tasks are performed. Option (A) Organising is the process/function of management. Option (C) Delegation is the transfer of authority from a superior to a subordinate. Option (D) Decentralisation is the systematic delegation of authority at all levels of management.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) संगठन ढाँचा है। संगठन ढाँचा वह औपचारिक रूपरेखा है जिसके अंतर्गत सभी प्रबन्धकीय और संचालन संबंधी कार्यों को निष्पादित किया जाता है।

questions.text:
रोहित एक फर्नीचर निर्माण कंपनी में प्रबंधक है। कंपनी दिसम्बर माह में वार्षिक सेल लगाती है जो बहुत ही प्रसिद्ध है। रोहित वार्षिक सेल के लिए प्रति वर्ष जून माह में ही अग्रिम रूप से उत्पादन योजना तैयार करता है । नियोजन के बाद, वह यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि पर्याप्त कामगार उपलब्ध हों और निरन्तर रूप से नज़र रखता है कि कार्य योजना के अनुरूप आगे बढ़ रहा है या नहीं । वे विपणन टीम को भी समय पर सूचना देता है ताकि वे अपने प्रचार अभियानों की योजना उसी के अनुरूप बना सकें।
उपर्युक्त स्थिति में समन्वय की जिस विशेषता पर प्रकाश डाला गया है, वह है :
questions.text_english:
Rohit is a manager at a furniture manufacturing company. The company holds an annual sale in the month of December, which is very popular. Rohit prepares the production plans for the annual sale well in advance, in the month of June every year. After planning, he ensures that enough workers are available and continuously monitors whether the work is progressing as scheduled or not. He also informs the marketing team well in time so that they can plan their promotional campaigns accordingly.
The feature of coordination highlighted in the above case is :

options.B: समन्वय एक निरन्तर चलने वाली प्रक्रिया है।
options.C: समन्वय एक सोचा समझा कार्य है ।
options.D: समन्वय सभी प्रबन्धकों का उत्तरदायित्व है ।

options_english.D: Coordination is the responsibility of all managers.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Coordination is a deliberate function. The key word in the case is deliberate — Rohit consciously and intentionally plans production in advance, ensures worker availability, monitors progress, and proactively informs the marketing team well in advance. This intentional and purposeful effort to synchronise different activities and departments highlights that coordination is a deliberate act and does not happen automatically. Option (A) is not reflected here as the case does not talk about coordination at all levels. Option (B) refers to continuity, which is also partially visible, but the dominant feature is the deliberate, intentional nature. Option (D) refers to coordination being the responsibility of all managers, which is not highlighted here.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) समन्वय एक सोचा समझा कार्य है। रोहित जानबूझकर पहले से योजना बनाकर, कामगारों की उपलब्धता सुनिश्चित करके और विपणन टीम को समय पर सूचित करके सभी कार्यों को समन्वित कर रहा है — यह जानबूझकर किया गया कार्य है।

questions.text: उस कथन का चयन कीजिए जो प्रभागीय ढाँचे के लाभ पर सही ढंग से प्रकाश डालता है :
questions.text_english: Choose the statement that correctly highlights the advantage of Divisional Structure :

options.A: इससे विस्तार और विकास में सुविधा होती है क्योंकि मौजूदा कार्यों को बाधित किए बिना नए विभाग जोड़े जा सकते हैं ।
options.B: यह प्रबंधकीय तथा संचालन संबंधी कुशलता की वृद्धि में सहायक होता है, परिणामस्वरूप लाभ में वृद्धि होती है।
options.C: इससे कर्मचारियों का प्रशिक्षण आसान हो जाता है क्योंकि सीमित कौशलों पर ध्यान केन्द्रित किया जाता है ।
options.D: इससे विभाग के अन्तर्गत सामंजस्य तथा नियंत्रण को बढ़ावा मिलता है क्योंकि निष्पादित किए जा रहे कार्यों में समानताएँ होती हैं।

options_english.A: It facilitates expansion and growth, as new divisions can be added without interrupting the existing operations.
options_english.B: It helps in increasing managerial and operational efficiency, resulting in increased profit.
options_english.C: It makes training of employees easier, as the focus is on a limited range of skills.
options_english.D: It promotes control and coordination within a department because of similarity in the tasks being performed.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). In a Divisional Structure, each division handles a specific product, market, or geography and operates somewhat independently. This makes it easy to add a new division without disrupting existing ones, facilitating expansion and growth. Option (B) describes an advantage of the Functional Structure, which increases specialisation and efficiency by grouping similar functions. Option (C) also describes an advantage of the Functional Structure where training is easier due to limited skill focus. Option (D) describes an advantage of the Functional Structure, where similarity of tasks within a department promotes better control and coordination.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। प्रभागीय ढाँचे में नई उत्पाद श्रेणियों या बाजारों के लिए नए विभाग जोड़े जा सकते हैं बिना वर्तमान कार्यों को बाधित किए, जिससे विस्तार एवं विकास आसान होता है।

questions.text: प्रबंध के निर्देशन कार्य की विशेषता से संबंधित गलत कथन को पहचानिए :
questions.text_english: Identify the incorrect statement with respect to the feature of Directing function of management :

options.A: निर्देशन एक निरंतर चलने वाली प्रक्रिया है
options.B: निर्देशन ऊपर से नीचे की ओर प्रवाहित होता है
options.C: निर्देशन केवल प्रबंध के उच्च स्तर पर ही निष्पादित होता है
options.D: निर्देशन क्रिया को आरंभ करता है

options_english.B: Directing flows from top to bottom
options_english.C: Directing takes place at top level of management only

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C), which is the incorrect statement. Directing does not take place only at the top level of management. It takes place at every level of management — top-level managers direct middle-level managers, middle-level managers direct supervisors, and supervisors direct workers. Directing permeates all levels of the organisation. Options (A), (B), and (D) are all correct features of directing: it is indeed a continuous process (it goes on throughout the life of an organisation), it flows from top to bottom (superior to subordinate), and it initiates action (actual work begins only after directions are given).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है जो गलत कथन है। निर्देशन केवल उच्च स्तर पर नहीं, बल्कि प्रबंध के प्रत्येक स्तर पर किया जाता है — उच्च स्तर, मध्य स्तर और निम्न स्तर सभी पर।

questions.text: कॉलम I में दिए गए प्रोत्साहन का कॉलम II में दिए गए उसके अर्थ से मिलान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Match the incentives given in Column I with their meanings given in Column II.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose the correct option from the following :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): 1-(iii), 2-(iv), 3-(ii), 4-(i). Job Security (1) means stability about future income and work — matched with (iii). Job Enrichment (2) means designing jobs with greater variety of work content and higher levels of knowledge and skill — matched with (iv). questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है: 1-(iii), 2-(iv), 3-(ii), 4-(i)। पद-सुरक्षा का अर्थ है भविष्य की आय और कार्य के बारे में स्थिरता (iii); पद-संवर्धन का अर्थ है विविध कार्यांश और उच्च ज्ञान वाले कार्यों की रूपरेखा (iv); जीवन-वृत्ति विकास अवसर का अर्थ है कौशल सुधार और पदोन्नति के अवसर (ii); कर्मचारी भागीदारी का अर्थ है निर्णय में सहभागिता (i)।

questions.text:
'लीड टाइम (कच्चे माल को पक्के माल में परिवर्तित करने का समय) जितना अधिक होगा, संग्रहित की जाने वाली सामग्री की मात्रा उतनी ही अधिक होगी और कार्यशील पूँजी की आवश्यकता भी उतनी ही अधिक होगी ।'
उपर्युक्त कथन में चर्चित कार्यशील पूँजी की आवश्यकता को प्रभावित करने वाला कारक है :
questions.text_english:
'The larger the lead time, the larger the quantity of material to be stored, and the larger shall be the amount of working capital required.'
The factor affecting the requirement of working capital discussed in the above statement is :

options.B: मुद्रास्फीति
options.C: कच्चे माल की उपलब्धता
options.D: उत्पादन चक्र

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Production cycle. The lead time referred to in the statement is the time taken to convert raw material into finished goods — this is essentially the production cycle or operating cycle. The longer the production cycle, the longer the time raw materials and work-in-progress are tied up, and the more working capital is needed to finance these. Option (A) Operating efficiency refers to how efficiently a business manages its operations. Option (B) Inflation refers to rising prices requiring more money for the same inputs. Option (C) Availability of raw material refers to whether materials are easily accessible.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) उत्पादन चक्र है। लीड टाइम वह समय है जो कच्चे माल को तैयार माल में बदलने में लगता है — यही उत्पादन चक्र है। उत्पादन चक्र जितना लंबा होगा, कार्यशील पूँजी की आवश्यकता उतनी ही अधिक होगी।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए :
कथन I : नियोजन एवं नियंत्रण दोनों ही भविष्योन्मुखी होने के साथ-साथ पीछे की ओर देखने वाले भी हैं ।
कथन II : नियोजन मूल्यांकनात्मक है, जबकि नियंत्रण निर्देशात्मक है ।
questions.text_english:
Read the following statements carefully :
Statement I : Planning and controlling are both forward-looking as well as backward-looking.
Statement II : Planning is evaluative, whereas controlling is prescriptive.
questions.instruction_line: दिए गए कथनों के आलोक में, निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.instruction_line_english: In the light of the given statements, choose the correct alternative from the following :

options.A: कथन I सत्य है तथा कथन II असत्य है ।
options.B: कथन I असत्य है तथा कथन II सत्य है ।
options.C: कथन I तथा कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं ।
options.D: कथन I तथा कथन II दोनों असत्य हैं ।

options_english.A: Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
options_english.B: Statement I is false and Statement II is true.
options_english.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options_english.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Statement I is true: Planning is forward-looking because it sets goals for the future. Controlling is backward-looking in the sense that it measures actual performance against pre-set standards (looking back at what happened). However, controlling is also forward-looking because corrective actions are taken to improve future performance. So both are forward-looking and backward-looking. Statement II is false: It is actually the reverse — Planning is prescriptive (it prescribes what is to be done), while controlling is evaluative (it evaluates whether actual performance matches the plans).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। कथन I सत्य है — नियोजन और नियंत्रण दोनों भविष्योन्मुखी और पश्चदर्शी हैं। कथन II असत्य है — वास्तव में नियोजन निर्देशात्मक (prescriptive) है और नियंत्रण मूल्यांकनात्मक (evaluative) है, न कि इसके विपरीत।

questions.text:
दिनकर ने, जो 'तारा लैम्पस' में महा प्रबन्धक है, देखा कि बढ़ती हुई लागतें कंपनी के लाभों को प्रभावित कर रही थीं । लाभों में वृद्धि के लिए, उसने लागतों को कम करने और उत्पादकता को बढ़ाने के बारे में सोचा । उसने कार्यप्रक्रियाओं के पुनव्यवस्थापन की योजना बनाई, श्रमिकों के कौशल के अनुसार कार्य सौंपे गए, पहले की अपेक्षा कर्मचारियों को अधिक स्पष्ट दिशा-निर्देश दिए गए तथा संगठन की गतिविधियों को नियमित रूप से नियंत्रित किया गया । इसके परिणामस्वरूप न केवल लागतों में कमी हुई अपितु उत्पादकता एवं लाभों में भी वृद्धि हुई ।
उपर्युक्त स्थिति में प्रबन्ध के महत्त्व के जिस बिंदु पर प्रकाश डाला गया है, वह है :
questions.text_english:
Dinkar, the General Manager at 'Tara Lamps' noticed that rising costs were affecting the company's profits. To increase the profits, he decided to reduce the costs and increase the productivity. He planned for rearrangement of work processes, assigned the tasks according to workers' skills, gave clearer directions to employees than before and regularly controlled the activities of the organisation. This not only resulted in cost reduction but also in increased productivity and profits.
The point of importance of management highlighted in the above case is :

options.A: प्रबंध गतिशील संगठन का निर्माण करता है
options.B: प्रबंध व्यक्तिगत उद्देश्यों की प्राप्ति में सहायक होता है
options.C: प्रबंध समाज के विकास में सहायक होता है
options.D: प्रबंध कार्यक्षमता में वृद्धि करता है

options_english.B: Management helps in achieving personal objectives
options_english.C: Management helps in the development of a society

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Management increases efficiency. The case clearly shows that through proper planning, assignment of tasks according to skills, clear directions, and effective control, Dinkar was able to reduce costs and increase productivity and profits. This is a classic example of how management increases efficiency — by using available resources optimally, minimising waste, and maximising output. Option (A) refers to creating a dynamic organisation that adapts to change. Option (B) refers to helping individual employees achieve their personal goals. Option (C) refers to management's contribution to society as a whole.

options.D: कथन I तथा कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं ।

options.B: वास्तविक निष्पादन का मापन, वास्तविक निष्पादन की मानकों से तुलना, विचलन विश्लेषण करना, सुधारात्मक कार्यवाही करना

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). The controlling process follows a logical sequence. 'Delicious Salads' was a company that supplied packaged salads to the supermarkets. Recently, the management noticed that a large amount of vegetables were getting spoiled every week. This was increasing the costs and reducing the profits because of which the company was not able to achieve its goals. To solve this, the Production Manager, Meera was asked to take charge of the situation and bring the wastage under control. Meera found that the vegetable cleaning, cutting and packing departments were working at their own pace, leading to the spoilage of vegetables. Within a month, 'Delicious Salads' was able to supply the salads with minimum wastage and achieve its goals.
Explain the two points of importance of the controlling function of management discussed in the above case.

key_points: Controlling helps in accomplishing organisational goals — by setting standards and monitoring performance, the company was able to achieve its targets.
Controlling helps in minimising wastage of resources — by coordinating the cleaning, cutting and packing departments with proper standards, wastage of vegetables was reduced significantly.

questions.solution: The two points of importance of the controlling function highlighted in the case are as follows. First, controlling helps in accomplishing organisational goals. In the case of 'Delicious Salads', Meera set coordinated performance standards for all departments. Each activity was performed in accordance with those standards, ensuring that all departments worked in sync. This helped the company achieve its goals of supplying salads with minimum wastage within just one month. Second, controlling helps in minimising wastage of resources. The vegetable cleaning, cutting and packing departments were working at their own pace, causing large-scale spoilage of vegetables. By setting proper standards and ensuring that each activity followed those standards, wastage was brought under control, costs were reduced, and profitability improved.

sub_questions.text_english: State any three points of difference between Formal organisation and Informal organisation.

key_points: Basis of formation: Formal organisation is deliberately created by management; informal organisation arises spontaneously from social interactions.
Nature: Formal organisation follows official rules and procedures; informal organisation is based on personal relationships and sentiments.
Authority: In formal organisation, authority flows through the official chain of command; in informal organisation, leadership is based on influence and acceptance.

sub_questions.solution: Formal and informal organisations differ on several important grounds. First, in terms of formation, formal organisation is deliberately and intentionally created by management to achieve specific organisational goals, whereas informal organisation emerges spontaneously from the social interactions, friendships and common interests among employees. Second, regarding their nature, formal organisation follows officially defined rules, procedures and policies, while informal organisation is based on personal relationships, sentiments and mutual understanding rather than written rules. Third, concerning authority and communication, in a formal organisation authority flows downward through the officially established chain of command, whereas in an informal organisation there is no defined chain of command — leadership is based on personal influence, and communication may flow in any direction through the grapevine.

sub_questions.text: एक संगठन के प्रभागीय ढाँचे तथा कार्यात्मक ढाँचे के बीच अंतभेद के किन्हीं तीन बिन्दुओं का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: State any three points of difference between Divisional structure and Functional structure of an organisation.

key_points: Basis of grouping: Divisional structure groups activities based on products/markets; functional structure groups activities based on functions.
Cost: Divisional structure leads to duplication of resources; functional structure is more economical.
Suitability: Divisional structure suits large, diversified organisations; functional structure suits smaller organisations with limited product range.

sub_questions.solution: Divisional and functional structures differ in three important ways. First, regarding the basis of grouping, a divisional structure organises activities around products, markets, or geographies — each division contains all the functions needed for that product, while a functional structure groups all similar functions (like production, marketing, finance) together regardless of the products involved. Second, in terms of cost and resource use, a divisional structure tends to involve duplication of resources because each division has its own functional specialists, making it more expensive; a functional structure is more economical as specialists are concentrated in one department and shared across the organisation. Third, concerning suitability, divisional structures are best suited for large, diversified organisations dealing with multiple products or markets, whereas functional structures work well for smaller organisations with a limited range of products and stable environments.

sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between Capital Market and Money Market on the basis of : (i) Participants (ii) Liquidity (iii) Duration

key_points: Participants: Capital market participants include retail investors, mutual funds, insurance companies, FIIs, and corporates; money market participants include RBI, commercial banks, LIC, and mutual funds.
Liquidity: Capital market instruments are less liquid than money market instruments.
Duration: Capital market deals in long-term securities (more than one year); money market deals in short-term instruments (less than one year).

sub_questions.solution: Capital Market and Money Market differ on the following three bases. First, regarding Participants, the capital market has a wider range of participants including retail investors, mutual funds, insurance companies, foreign institutional investors (FIIs), and business firms. In contrast, the money market is dominated by institutional participants such as the Reserve Bank of India, commercial banks, Life Insurance Corporation, and mutual funds — the general public rarely participates directly. Second, concerning Liquidity, money market instruments are highly liquid because they are short-term and can be converted to cash very quickly. Capital market instruments such as equity shares and long-term bonds are relatively less liquid, though the secondary market provides some liquidity. Third, in terms of Duration, capital market instruments have a maturity period of more than one year and are used to raise long-term funds for investment in fixed assets. Money market instruments have a maturity of less than one year and are used to meet short-term working capital needs.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain how the following factors affect the requirements of fixed capital of a company : (i) Nature of the business (ii) Technology upgradation (iii) Level of collaboration

key_points: Nature of business: Manufacturing companies require more fixed capital than trading companies.
Technology upgradation: Technology-intensive industries require higher fixed capital investment.
Level of collaboration: Higher levels of outsourcing or collaboration reduce the need for own fixed capital.

sub_questions.solution: The requirement of fixed capital is influenced by the following factors. First, Nature of the Business plays a crucial role. Manufacturing companies require heavy investment in fixed assets like plant, machinery, land and buildings, so they need large amounts of fixed capital. Trading companies, on the other hand, require much less fixed capital as they primarily need storage and office space rather than manufacturing equipment. Second, Technology Upgradation affects fixed capital needs significantly. Industries that require sophisticated, high-technology equipment need to invest heavily in fixed assets, increasing their fixed capital requirement. Moreover, when technology changes rapidly, companies need to replace outdated machinery more frequently, which further increases the need for fixed capital. Third, Level of Collaboration or outsourcing reduces fixed capital requirements. A company that outsources a significant portion of its production activities does not need to own all the machinery and equipment itself, thereby reducing its own fixed capital investment. Greater collaboration means shared resources and lower individual fixed capital needs.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following features of principles of management : (i) Cause and effect relationship (ii) Contingent

key_points: Cause and effect relationship — principles establish a relationship between a cause and its probable effect, helping managers predict outcomes.
Contingent — principles are not absolute; their application depends on the prevailing situation and conditions.

sub_questions.solution: The principles of management have the following two features. First, Cause and Effect Relationship: Principles of management establish a relationship between a cause and its effect. They help managers understand which managerial action (cause) is likely to produce a particular result (effect). For instance, if the principle of Division of Work is applied, the expected effect is increased efficiency and better productivity. This cause-and-effect relationship makes the principles useful as guidelines for managerial decisions. However, unlike the exact laws of physical sciences, the cause-and-effect relationship in management may not be perfectly precise because human behaviour is complex and unpredictable. Second, Contingent: Management principles are not absolute or universal in the sense that they cannot be applied blindly in all situations. Their application is contingent — that is, it depends on the prevailing situation, the nature of the organisation, and the specific circumstances. For example, the principle of Centralisation may work well in a small firm but may not be appropriate for a large multinational corporation. Managers must exercise judgement in deciding which principles to apply and to what extent, based on the context they face.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following techniques of scientific management : (i) Motion Study (ii) Differential Piece Wage System

key_points: Motion Study — eliminating unnecessary movements to find the best way to do a job.
Differential Piece Wage System — efficient workers receive higher wages per piece; inefficient workers receive lower wages.

sub_questions.solution: The following two techniques of scientific management were developed by F.W. Taylor. First, Motion Study: Motion study refers to a careful analysis of the movements made by a worker while performing a task. Taylor observed that workers often made unnecessary, wasteful motions that slowed down their work. By systematically studying and eliminating such unnecessary movements, the most efficient way to perform a task could be identified. Motion study reduces fatigue, saves time, and increases productivity. For example, studying the movements of bricklayers led to a reduction in the number of motions needed per brick, significantly increasing their output. Second, Differential Piece Wage System: This is a wage payment technique designed to motivate workers to increase their output. Under this system, two different piece rates are set — a higher rate for workers who achieve or exceed the standard output, and a lower rate for those who fail to meet the standard. An efficient worker who completes 120 bricks in an hour (meeting the standard) gets paid at the higher rate, while an inefficient worker who completes only 80 bricks gets paid at the lower rate. This creates a strong financial incentive for workers to improve their efficiency.

questions.text: उपभोक्ता संरक्षण अधिनियम, 2019 के अंतर्गत एक उपभोक्ता के किन्हीं चार उत्तरदायित्वों का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: State any four responsibilities of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

key_points: Be aware about goods and services before purchasing.
Buy only standardised goods and look for quality certifications (ISI, Agmark, etc.).
File complaints in case of defective goods or services.
Be honest and avoid black market purchases.

questions.solution: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a consumer has the following four important responsibilities. First, a consumer must be aware and well-informed about the quality, quantity, price, and standards of goods and services before making a purchase. An informed consumer is less likely to be deceived. Second, a consumer should buy only standardised goods and insist on quality marks such as ISI, Agmark, Hallmark, or FPO, as these marks assure the quality and safety of products. Third, a consumer should file a complaint whenever he encounters defective goods, deficient services, or unfair trade practices. Filing complaints not only helps the individual but also protects other consumers from similar exploitation. Fourth, a consumer must be honest and avoid purchasing goods from the black market or without proper receipts. Consumers should insist on cash memos and proper bills, as these serve as evidence in case of any dispute or complaint.

questions.text_english:
Arjun and Neha were close friends. They had studied together in the same school. After completing their higher education, both of them joined a company named 'Apex Ltd.' in different roles, based on their qualifications. Arjun's role involved analysing the business environment and its implications for the survival of the firm. He was also responsible for the welfare and survival of the organisation. Neha, on the other hand, was heading the marketing department in the organisation. Her responsibility was to ensure that her department had the necessary personnel. In addition to many other responsibilities, she had to motivate them to achieve desired objectives.
Apart from the functions mentioned in the above case, state two more functions each for Arjun and Neha that they would perform at the level at which they are working.

key_points: Arjun — Top Level: (1) Setting overall organisational goals and objectives; (2) Communicating with shareholders, government and other stakeholders.
Neha — Middle Level: (1) Training and developing subordinates; (2) Coordinating with other departments to achieve goals.

questions.solution:
Arjun is clearly working at the Top Level of management, as his role involves analysing the business environment for the firm's survival and being responsible for the overall welfare of the organisation. Two additional functions that Arjun would perform at the top level are: first, setting the overall goals and long-term objectives of the organisation, formulating broad policies and strategic plans that determine the direction of the company; and second, being accountable to shareholders and the board of directors, communicating with external stakeholders such as the government, investors, and the public to maintain the organisation's reputation and relationships.

Neha is working at the Middle Level of management as she is heading the marketing department. Two additional functions that Neha would perform at this level are: first, training and developing the employees in her department so that they acquire the skills and knowledge needed to meet the department's objectives; and second, interpreting and communicating top-level policies to her departmental team, as well as coordinating with other departments such as production and finance to ensure that marketing goals are achieved effectively.

जागरूकता की बढ़ती हुई आवश्यकता को देखते हुए, इस एनजीओ ने उपभोक्ता की समस्याओं, कानूनी रिपोर्ट देना, उपलब्ध राहतों तथा उपभोक्ता हित के अन्य विषयों के संबंध में ज्ञान प्रदान करने के लिए पत्रिकाओं एवं प्रकाशनों को प्रकाशित करना आरंभ किया । ये प्रकाशन अत्यधिक लोकप्रिय हो गए और लोगों ने मार्गदर्शन के लिए एनजीओ से सम्पर्क करना आरंभ कर दिया ।

questions.text_english:
'Sabka Consumer Forum', a well-known non-governmental organisation (NGO), has been working for the welfare of the consumers. Its main aim is to educate the general public about consumer rights by organising training programmes, seminars and workshops.
Seeing the growing need for awareness, the NGO started publishing periodicals and other publications to impart knowledge about consumer problems, legal reporting, reliefs available and other matters of consumer interest. These publications became very popular and people began approaching the NGO for guidance.
One day, a group of residents from a nearby housing society approached 'Sabka Consumer Forum'. They had purchased water purifiers from a company, which turned out to be defective. Even after repeated complaints, the company had failed to respond. 'Sabka Consumer Forum' studied the case and decided to file a complaint on behalf of the consumers in the appropriate consumer court.
Apart from the functions mentioned in the above case, state any four other functions which may be performed by 'Sabka Consumer Forum' for protecting and promoting consumer interests.

key_points: Collecting and analysing data about market frauds and publishing reports for public awareness.
Providing legal aid and assistance to consumers in filing complaints.
Conducting product testing and quality analysis to identify defective or substandard products.
Lobbying and advocating with government and regulatory bodies for stronger consumer protection laws.

questions.solution: Apart from the functions already mentioned in the case (educating consumers through training programmes and seminars, publishing periodicals, and filing complaints on behalf of consumers), 'Sabka Consumer Forum' can perform the following four additional functions for protecting and promoting consumer interests. First, it can collect and analyse data on market malpractices, fraudulent advertising, adulteration, and unfair trade practices and publish reports to alert consumers and the public. Second, it can provide legal aid and assistance to individual consumers who cannot afford legal representation, helping them navigate the consumer redressal system and assert their rights. Third, it can conduct product testing and quality analysis by arranging for independent testing of goods sold in the market, and warn consumers about substandard or unsafe products. Fourth, it can engage in lobbying and advocacy by representing consumer interests before government bodies, regulatory authorities, and the legislature, pushing for the formulation of stronger consumer protection laws and more effective enforcement mechanisms.

रिया हाथ से बनी मोमबत्तियों को बेचने का ऑनलाइन व्यवसाय चला रही है। दीवाली के सीज़न में उसकी हाथ से बनी सुगंधित मोमबत्तियों की माँग बहुत अधिक बढ़ जाती है। दीवाली से एक महीने पहले उपहार स्टोर्स की एक श्रृंखला (शहर में और उसके आस-पास) से उसने एक बड़ा आदेश प्राप्त किया । रिया ने तुरंत आदेश के विवरण देखे और उसका प्रक्रियण किया । वह यह जानती थी कि आदेशों का सही एवं शीघ्र प्रक्रियण करना महत्त्वपूर्ण होता है जिसकी अनुपस्थिति में उपभोक्ताओं को वस्तुएँ देर से या गलत मात्रा में पहुँचेंगी या वर्णन के अनुसार नहीं होंगी। आदेश के प्रक्रियण के बाद रिया ने अपनी कार्यशाला से डिब्बों को लाने के लिए एक वाहन की व्यवस्था की। वह जानती थी कि वस्तुएँ ग्राहकों तक केवल तभी पहुँच सकती हैं जब उन्हें भौतिक रूप से उत्पादन के स्थान से बिक्री के स्थान तक ले जाया जाएगा। त्योहार की भीड़-भाड़ से काफी पहले ही वाहन ने आदेश को उपहार श्रृंखला के भंडारगृह में पहुँचा दिया ।

questions.text_english:
Rhea runs an online business selling handmade candles. During the Diwali season, the demand for her handmade scented candles increases a lot. A month before Diwali, she received a big order from a chain of gift stores in and around the city. Rhea immediately checked the order details and processed it. She was aware that it was important to provide for accurate and speedy processing of orders, in the absence of which goods would reach the customers late or in the wrong quantity or specifications. After processing the order, Rhea arranged a vehicle to pick up the cartons from her workshop. She knew that the products can reach the customers only when they are physically moved from the place of production to the place of sale. The vehicle delivered the order at the gift chain's warehouse well before the festive rush.
(a) Identify the two components of physical distribution that Rhea managed effectively.
(b) Explain the other two components of physical distribution that Rhea needs to work on.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the two components of physical distribution that Rhea managed effectively.

key_points: Order Processing — Rhea immediately checked order details and processed the order accurately and speedily.
Transportation — Rhea arranged a vehicle to physically move the goods from her workshop to the gift chain's warehouse.

sub_questions.solution: The two components of physical distribution that Rhea managed effectively are Order Processing and Transportation. Rhea immediately checked the order details and processed it accurately and speedily, ensuring goods would reach customers in the right quantity and as per specifications — this is order processing. She also arranged a vehicle to physically move the goods from her workshop to the gift chain's warehouse well before the festive rush — this is transportation.

sub_questions.text: भौतिक वितरण के दो अन्य घटकों को समझाइए जिन पर रिया को काम करने की आवश्यकता है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the other two components of physical distribution that Rhea needs to work on.

key_points: Warehousing — storing goods until they are needed by the customer.
Inventory Management — maintaining optimum stock levels to meet customer demand without overstocking.

sub_questions.solution: The other two components of physical distribution that Rhea needs to work on are Warehousing and Inventory Management. Warehousing refers to the process of storing goods from the time of their production until the time they are needed by consumers. Since Rhea's business is seasonal and she receives large orders during Diwali, she needs proper storage facilities to keep her finished candles safe until they are dispatched. Inventory Management refers to maintaining an optimum level of stock — not too much (which would tie up capital and risk wastage) and not too little (which could result in stockouts and failure to fulfil orders). For Rhea, effective inventory management during the festive season would ensure she has enough candles ready to meet demand without incurring unnecessary costs.

sub_questions.solution: Rajan sold his shares in the Secondary Market, also known as the Stock Exchange. Since 'Neo Appliances Ltd.' shares were already issued previously and Rajan was selling existing shares (not newly issued ones), this transaction took place in the secondary market.

sub_questions.solution: The function of the secondary market (stock exchange) that facilitated Rajan in selling his shares is Providing Liquidity to Investors. 'Alpha Electronics' had recently received a large order for the supply of electronic control panels. The management was under pressure to deliver it on time. When one of the production lines started malfunctioning, the Production Manager, Suresh, was concerned. Although 'Alpha Electronics' was an organisation with highly centralised pattern where free communication was not encouraged. Suresh, still decided to call his senior technician, Manoj, to understand the problem. Suresh had the reputation of being unapproachable. He was conscious of his seniority and position so he rarely encouraged his subordinates to speak freely. Manoj was nervous as the production line was damaged due to his own negligence and he thought sharing it with his senior, Suresh, would adversely affect his interests. Anyhow, he had to go to Suresh's office. When Manoj entered Suresh's office, he saw that Suresh was pre-occupied with an important file before him. Suresh asked Manoj to explain what the problem was. Manoj reluctantly started explaining, but he felt that Suresh wasn't listening to him. So Manoj did not share the complete information and the problem in the production line could not be rectified on time.
Identify and explain four communication barriers discussed in the above case.

key_points: Organisational barrier — highly centralised organisation where free communication was not encouraged.
Status-consciousness barrier — Suresh was conscious of his seniority and rarely encouraged subordinates to speak freely.
Fear barrier — Manoj feared that sharing information about his own negligence would harm his interests.
Inattentive listening — Suresh was pre-occupied with an important file and was not listening attentively to Manoj.

questions.solution:
The four communication barriers discussed in the case of 'Alpha Electronics' are as follows.

First, Organisational Barrier: 'Alpha Electronics' was described as a highly centralised organisation where free communication was not encouraged. When communication is restricted by the formal structure and hierarchy, important information does not flow freely across levels. This organisational culture prevented open dialogue and hindered the timely resolution of the production line problem.

Second, Status-Consciousness (or Superior-Subordinate Relationship Barrier): Suresh was conscious of his seniority and position, and he rarely encouraged subordinates to speak openly. When a superior creates an aura of unapproachability, subordinates feel hesitant to communicate freely. This barrier — known as a psychological or organisational barrier arising from status differences — prevented Manoj from communicating the complete truth to Suresh.

Third, Fear of Consequences (Psychological Barrier): Manoj was nervous because the production line damage was caused by his own negligence. He feared that revealing the complete information would adversely affect his personal interests, such as his job or reputation. This emotional and psychological barrier — fear of punishment or negative consequences — led Manoj to withhold critical information, directly causing the failure to solve the problem in time.

Fourth, Inattentive Listening (Psychological Barrier): When Manoj entered Suresh's office, Suresh was already engaged with an important file and was not listening properly. Poor listening is a major communication barrier. When the receiver is distracted or inattentive, the message is not properly understood, resulting in miscommunication or incomplete information exchange.

(a) Explain the following points of limitations of planning : (i) Planning reduces creativity (ii) Planning leads to rigidity (iii) Planning does not guarantee success
OR
(b) Explain the following points of importance of organising : (i) Adaptation to change (ii) Effective administration (iii) Expansion and growth

sub_questions.text: नियोजन की सीमाओं के निम्नलिखित बिन्दुओं को समझाइए : (i) नियोजन रचनात्मकता को कम करता है (ii) नियोजन दृढ़ता उत्पन्न करता है (iii) नियोजन सफलता का आश्वासन नहीं है
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following points of limitations of planning : (i) Planning reduces creativity (ii) Planning leads to rigidity (iii) Planning does not guarantee success

key_points: Planning reduces creativity — middle and lower level managers follow pre-set plans and cannot suggest new approaches.
Planning leads to rigidity — once a plan is made, managers are reluctant to deviate from it even when circumstances change.
Planning does not guarantee success — plans may fail if based on incorrect assumptions or if the environment changes drastically.

sub_questions.solution:
Planning, despite its many advantages, suffers from the following three limitations.

First, Planning Reduces Creativity: Planning establishes a framework within which all activities must be carried out. Once top-level management formulates plans, middle and lower level managers are expected to implement them without deviation. This leaves little room for employees at lower levels to suggest new ideas, take initiatives, or think creatively. Over time, planning can make an organisation rigid and stifle the spirit of innovation among employees, as everyone is expected to follow the pre-determined course of action.

Second, Planning Leads to Rigidity: Once a plan is made and resources are committed, managers become reluctant to change their course of action even when circumstances demand it. The existence of a detailed plan can create inflexibility in the organisation. For instance, if a plan requires a specific method of production, managers may not adopt a better method even if it becomes available, simply because it was not part of the original plan. This rigidity can be harmful, especially in dynamic and fast-changing business environments.

Third, Planning Does Not Guarantee Success: Planning provides a roadmap for action, but it does not assure success. Plans are based on forecasts and assumptions about the future, which may turn out to be incorrect. A company may prepare a very thorough and detailed plan, yet still fail to achieve its goals if the business environment changes unexpectedly — due to economic downturns, natural disasters, or technological disruptions. Success depends not only on good planning but also on effective implementation, which cannot be guaranteed.

sub_questions.text: संगठन के महत्त्व के निम्नलिखित बिन्दुओं को समझाइए : (i) परिवर्तनों का अनुकूलन (ii) प्रभावी प्रशासन (iii) विस्तार एवं विकास
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following points of importance of organising : (i) Adaptation to change (ii) Effective administration (iii) Expansion and growth

key_points: Adaptation to change — a well-structured organisation can easily restructure to respond to changing business needs.
Effective administration — clear role definition and authority structure enables smooth administration.
Expansion and growth — organising enables the organisation to take on new activities without disrupting existing ones.

sub_questions.solution:
Organising is one of the most important functions of management. Its importance is highlighted through the following three points.

First, Adaptation to Change: A well-designed organisational structure provides the flexibility to adapt to changes in the business environment. When external factors such as market conditions, technology, or government policies change, the organisation can modify its structure — by adding new departments, reassigning roles, or redefining authority relationships — without disrupting ongoing operations. This ability to restructure makes the organisation resilient and capable of surviving in a dynamic environment.

Second, Effective Administration: Organising defines the roles and responsibilities of each employee clearly. When every person knows what they are supposed to do and to whom they are accountable, administration becomes smooth and efficient. There is no confusion about tasks, duplication of efforts is avoided, and coordination among different departments becomes easier. Clear lines of authority also ensure that decisions are taken at the right level and implemented quickly, leading to effective overall administration.

Third, Expansion and Growth: A sound organisational structure supports the growth and expansion of the enterprise. As the business grows, new products can be added, new markets can be entered, and new departments can be created without disturbing the existing structure. The divisional structure, for example, allows a company to add a new product division independently. A well-organised firm can take on larger volumes of work and a wider variety of activities, enabling it to grow sustainably over time.

This financial year, the profits of the company increased manifold as the company introduced a new range of baked snacks that became very popular. As the year came to an end, the company had to decide how much dividend to pay to its shareholders. In view of the above and with the understanding that investors, in general, view an increase in dividend as good news and stock prices react positively to it, the Board of Directors were keen on declaring a high dividend. However, the Chief Finance Officer of the company pointed out that they need to keep many considerations in mind before declaring dividend. sub_questions.text_english: Identify and explain any two factors affecting dividend decision that would have influenced the decision of the Board of Directors to pay a high dividend.

key_points: Earnings — the company's profits increased manifold, providing sufficient earnings to distribute as dividend.
Stability of Dividends / Shareholders' Preferences — investors expect dividend increases when profits are high; a higher dividend improves share price.

sub_questions.solution: The two factors that influenced the Board of Directors to declare a high dividend are as follows. First, Earnings or Profitability: The company's profits increased manifold during the year due to the success of its new baked snacks range. Since dividends can only be paid out of current or past profits, higher earnings create a larger pool of funds available for distribution. The Board naturally considered declaring a high dividend because the company had sufficient earnings to support it. Second, Stability of Dividends or Preference of Shareholders: The Board was aware that investors generally view an increase in dividend as a positive signal, and that share prices tend to react positively to higher dividends. Companies that maintain or increase their dividend payments are perceived as financially healthy and confident. This positive impact on share valuation and shareholder satisfaction motivated the Board to declare a higher dividend.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify and explain any two factors to which the Chief Finance Officer drew the attention of the Board of Directors.

key_points: Contractual constraints / Loan agreement — the loan agreement contained a clause restricting dividend payment.
Cash flow / Liquidity — large amounts were tied up in receivables, making cash unavailable for dividend payment.
Growth prospects / Investment opportunities — the company planned to expand into the breakfast cereal market, requiring retained earnings.

sub_questions.solution: The Chief Finance Officer drew the Board's attention to the following two factors that would limit the high dividend payout. First, Contractual Constraints (Loan Covenant): The company had taken a loan that contained a specific clause restricting the payment of dividends. Lenders sometimes impose such conditions to protect their interest, ensuring that the company does not weaken its financial position by paying out large sums as dividends. This legal restriction meant that irrespective of the level of profits, the company could not freely declare dividends beyond the stipulated limit without violating the loan agreement. Second, Cash Flow Position (Liquidity): Even though the company's accounting profits were high, a large amount of money was tied up in debtors (accounts receivable) and had not yet been collected. Dividend payment requires actual cash, not just reported profits. Without sufficient liquid funds, declaring a high dividend would strain the company's cash flow and could create financial difficulties in meeting day-to-day operational needs. The CFO also pointed to the company's growth plan — expansion into the breakfast cereal market would require heavy investment, and retaining more earnings now would be necessary to finance this project without excessive borrowing.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following steps in the process of staffing : (i) Selection (ii) Promotion and Career Planning (iii) Compensation

key_points: Selection — choosing the most suitable candidate from the pool of applicants through tests and interviews.
Promotion and Career Planning — providing growth opportunities within the organisation.
Compensation — determining and paying fair wages and salaries.

sub_questions.solution:
The following three steps in the staffing process are explained below.

First, Selection: Selection is the process of identifying and choosing the most suitable candidate from the pool of applicants generated through recruitment. It involves a series of screening steps such as preliminary interview, application form screening, selection tests (aptitude, intelligence, personality), employment interviews, medical examination, and reference checks. The objective is to match the right person with the right job. Selection is often called a negative process because it involves rejection of unsuitable candidates at various stages.

Second, Promotion and Career Planning: Once an employee joins the organisation, the management must plan for their growth and advancement. Promotion refers to moving an employee to a higher position with greater responsibilities, better pay, and higher status. Career planning involves laying out a path for the employee's long-term development — identifying which positions they may occupy over their career and what skills they will need to develop. A well-designed promotion and career planning system motivates employees to perform better and reduces staff turnover by providing a clear future within the organisation.

Third, Compensation: Compensation refers to the monetary and non-monetary rewards given to employees in exchange for their services. It includes basic salary or wages, allowances, bonuses, and other benefits such as health insurance or provident fund contributions. A fair and competitive compensation package is essential to attract and retain talented employees. Compensation must be designed to satisfy employees' basic needs while also recognising and rewarding superior performance.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following external sources of recruitment : (i) Direct Recruitment (ii) Casual Callers (iii) Labour Contractors

key_points: Direct Recruitment — a notice is placed at the factory gate and unskilled workers are recruited directly.
Casual Callers — candidates who apply on their own initiative without any advertisement.
Labour Contractors — middlemen who supply workers to organisations on a contractual basis.

sub_questions.solution:
The following three external sources of recruitment are explained below.

First, Direct Recruitment: In this method, the organisation puts up a notice at the factory gate or premises specifying the jobs available and the qualifications required. Interested candidates gather and are selected on the spot, often for unskilled or semi-skilled positions. This method is simple, quick, and inexpensive. It is commonly used in manufacturing or production units where a large number of unskilled labourers are needed at short notice.

Second, Casual Callers (Unsolicited Applicants/Waiting List): Many reputed organisations receive applications from potential candidates on their own initiative, even without any active recruitment drive. These are called casual callers. The organisation maintains a database of such unsolicited applications. When a vacancy arises, the HR department contacts suitable candidates from this pool. This method saves time and cost as the organisation does not need to advertise or conduct an extensive recruitment process.

Third, Labour Contractors: In this method, the organisation engages a labour contractor — a middleman — who maintains contacts with workers, particularly in rural areas or among migrant labour communities. The contractor provides the required number of workers to the organisation on a contractual basis. This method is used especially when temporary, seasonal, or contractual workers are needed. However, a disadvantage is that if the contractor leaves the organisation, the workers supplied by him may also leave, creating uncertainty.
